messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High GPU queue length detected in us-east-1. queue_len=8200, avg_latency=920ms, gpu_util=98%. Paging oncall.
Maya (oncall): Acked. jumping in. any customer-facing errors?
Tom (infra): Seeing a spike in 429s from hosted API and many requests queued. 5% of requests failing with 429s, tail latency > 1s. Autoscaler is saturated at 12 pods (max_replicas). Logs show failed scale attempts: 
```
Error: reached max replicas limit: cannot scale above 12
autoscaler_event: scale_failed
```
Jordan (runtime): I just deployed a tweak to continuous batching 18m ago — increased batch_window_ms from 80 -> 220 and reduced prefix_cache_ttl from 600 -> 60 to test cache evictions. Might be related.
Sanjay (serving): That TTL change would explain a prefix cache miss storm. More KV cache misses => more KV lookups add latency and block batching throughput.
Maya (oncall): Good catch. Rollback possible? If we roll back batching params we might relieve queue. But autoscaler limit is still a blocker.
Tom (infra): Short-term mitigation: bump autoscaler max_replicas to 24 and increase node pool ephemeral capacity. I'll run the change.
Tom (infra): Running command: 
```
kubectl patch hpa/gpu-inference-autoscaler -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":24}]'
```
deploy-bot: Deploy started for config rollback by Jordan (runtime).
Jordan (runtime): Opening rollback PR now to restore continuous batching to previous values and revert prefix_cache_ttl. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4523
Maya (oncall): After Tom's scale change, queue length dropped from 8200 -> 2100 in ~2m. Latency down to ~480ms. Still above SLO but improving.
Sanjay (serving): While we have headroom, also suggest decreasing batch_window_ms back to 80 and re-enable prefix cache 600s. I'll prepare the config snippet to apply.
Jordan (runtime): Config to apply (will revert to previous): 
```
continuous_batching:
  batch_window_ms: 80
  max_batch_size: 64
prefix_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 600
  max_entries: 50000
```
Jordan (runtime): Applying rollback now.
deploy-bot: Rollback deploy succeeded. config-version: v2026-11-128.
Maya (oncall): Observing metrics: queue_len -> 600 within 4m post-rollback, 429s reduced to ~0.8%, avg_gen_latency ~320ms.
Tom (infra): Autoscaler change is live. We increased max_replicas and temporarily allowed burst scale. I'll monitor node quotas.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact summary for postmortem: ~18 minutes of elevated errors/latency, primary impact: hosted text-generation customers in us-east-1 saw 3-7% increased error rate and tail latency spikes. No Dedicated customers reported SLA violations yet.
Sanjay (serving): Root cause hypothesis: config regression in continuous batching + aggressive prefix_cache_ttl reduction caused cache miss storm and increased per-request work, which combined with autoscaler max cap caused backlog and throttling.
Jordan (runtime): I'll add guardrails: require canary for batching param changes and set alert if queue_len > 1000 after deploy. Also will add a validation check preventing prefix_cache_ttl < 300s without review.
Maya (oncall): Actions taken: 1) Temporary autoscaler max increased to 24 (Tom) 2) Rolled back batching/prefix cache (Jordan) 3) Monitoring thresholds tightened (Jordan) 4) Notified customers via status page; CS notified top 10 customers.
Tom (infra): Leaving the autoscaler max at 24 for 1h then revert to normal 12 once stable.
deploy-bot: Pager closed? No further alerts.
Maya (oncall): I'll escalate to P1 postmortem and assign owners: Jordan -> runtime fix/PR, Tom -> autoscaler guard, Sanjay -> cache metrics dashboard update. I'll file incident ticket.
Jordan (runtime): Filing postmortem now: ITP-2026-1189. Will include metric diffs, config diff, and suggested automated rollback policy.
Maya (oncall): Thanks team. marking resolved for on-call. :thumbsup:
Tom (infra): +1. logging incident timeline to ops-runbook.
Sanjay (serving): Follow-up: patch to prefix cache eviction logic to avoid full miss storms when TTL is low.
Maya (oncall): End of thread.
